result.topic_en: Simplification of the moment (integral) for the parabolic arc FH between two points, and the remark that when gg < fh two minimizing parabolic arcs (two projectile trajectories) exist from F to H.

Quod si haec posterior fractio multiplicetur supra et infra
per $f+h-2\sqrt{\ldots}$ prodibit ejus numerator
$=(f+h)(2gg+ff+hh)-2(f+h)(fh-gg)$
$+(2fh-ff-hh-4gg)\sqrt{\ldots}$
qui reducitur ad hanc formam:
$(f+h)(4gg+(h-f)^2)-(4gg+(h-f)^2)\sqrt{\ldots}$
$=(4gg+(h-f)^2)(f+h-\sqrt{\ldots})$.
At vero denominator prodibit $(h-f)^2+4gg$, sicque com-
mode evenit ut evadat momentum quaesitum $=\frac{2g}{3\sqrt{a}}(f+h-\sqrt{\ldots})$.
Quare cum $\sqrt{a}=\frac{g}{\sqrt{(f+h+2\sqrt{\ldots})}}$, erit hoc momentum pro arcu FH
$=\frac{2}{3}(f+h-\sqrt{\ldots})(\sqrt{f+h+2\sqrt{\ldots}})$.

items.quote: Quoties ergo fuerit $gg<fh$, ob signum radicale semper duo exhiberi poterunt minima, sive ab F ad H binos arcus parabolicos ducere licebit.
items.english: Therefore whenever gg < fh, because of the radical sign two minima can always be exhibited, i.e. two parabolic arcs may be drawn from F to H.

items.quote: ex puncto F duplici modo corpus cum celeritate altitudini $Ff$ debita ita projici poterit, ut punctum H feriat.
items.english: From point F a body with the velocity due to height Ff can be projected in two ways so as to strike point H.

items.quote: Ex quo facile intelligitur, hoc fieri non posse, nisi punctum H ultra certam distantiam fuerit remotum
items.english: From which it is easily understood that this cannot happen unless point H is removed beyond a certain distance
